record.paper_title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
record.original_question: Besides being a critical configuration of the energy, do the zeros of the Freud-type orthogonal polynomials preserve any of the other equilibrium notions discussed earlier for classical electrostatic models?

evidence.quote: Is still any other type of equilibria discussed in Section 2 preserved in this case (beside the critical point of the energy)? This is also an open question.

artifact.status_search_result: The literature on electrostatic interpretations of zeros of Freud-type orthogonal polynomials establishes that the zeros are critical points of the associated discrete logarithmic energy in the external field $Q$, with the energy expressible via recursion coefficients and its large-$n$ limit studied. However, no source located in the search confirms that additional equilibrium notions (global/local minimum, coordinatewise minimization, force-balance characterization analogous to the classical Stieltjes picture) have been verified for general Freud weights. The question of which further equilibrium properties extend from the classical to the Freud-type case appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An electrostatic interpretation of the zeros of the Freud-type orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: The zeros of the Freud-type orthogonal polynomials are critical points of the energy function; total energy is computed via recursion coefficients with limit studied as n tends to infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Only the critical-point property is established for Freud-type zeros; stronger equilibrium properties are not asserted.

status_evidence.title: An electrostatics model for zeros of general orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Zeros of general orthogonal polynomials determine equilibrium positions of movable unit charges in an external field; equilibrium is the zero gradient, stable equilibrium a global minimum.
status_evidence.claim: Distinguishes critical points from stable (minimizing) equilibria in the general OP setting.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic interpretation of zeros of orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of electrostatic models; classical orthogonal polynomials enjoy stronger equilibrium characterizations than general weights.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that extending classical equilibrium properties to general (e.g., Freud) weights is nontrivial and not fully resolved.
